There are some places in India that are so traveller-friendly and yet so enchanting and hassle-free as mountain-framed Leh. Built with whitewashed houses, the Old Town is dominated by steep rocky ridge topped by an imposing Tibetan-style palace and fort. Beneath, the bazaar area is draped in a thick veneer of tour agencies, souvenir shops and tandoori-pizza restaurants, but a web of lanes quickly fans out into a green suburban patchwork of irrigated barley fields. Here, gushing streams and narrow footpaths link traditionally styled Ladakhi garden homes that double as charming, inexpensive guesthouses. Leh’s a place that’s all too easy to fall in love with – but take things very easy on arrival as the altitude requires a few days' acclimatisation before you can safely start enjoying the area's gamut of adventure activities. We were there for 4 days but my cousin faced an acute respiratory problem due to low oxygen level. This place is a hell lot of adventure.
